name: basten
author: animals-and-nature agent
description:
basten (direction: animals and nature) - A FISH TANK, AND THE FISH THAT ARE NIBBLING THE WEEDS. PRIVATE; never shown to players.

CLUE = "<plants>/<N>". <plants> is the gravel bed read left to right, 28-34 characters: "." is bare gravel and a digit 1-3 is a water plant of that height growing at that column. 5-8 plants, always at least 4 columns apart, never within 3 columns of either end, total height >= 10 with at least 3 plants taller than 1. N is 2..8.

ANSWER = the finished tank. Line 1 is the water surface, "~" repeated to the clue's width. The last line is the gravel, "#" repeated to the same width. Between them are D water rows, 4 <= D <= 6, each exactly as wide. Each plant of height h fills the bottom h water rows of its own column with "|"; every other cell is "." (open water) or part of a fish. A fish is "><>" (swimming right, nose on the right) or "<><" (swimming left, nose on the left), three cells in one row, never over a plant, never touching another fish, and every water row must hold at least one fish. Whitespace is free: the scorer reads the answer with .split(), so blank lines, indentation and trailing spaces do not matter.

RULE. score = 1 iff the picture is well formed as above AND (2) the number of distinct PLANT SPOTS being nibbled is exactly N - a plant spot is one "|" cell, and it is nibbled when the cell in front of some fish's nose is that cell, i.e. the picture shows "><>|" or "|<><" - AND (3) at least one spot is nibbled from BOTH sides at once, i.e. "><>|<><" occurs somewhere. Note the difference between clause 2 and "count the nibbling fish": a spot eaten from both sides is ONE spot but TWO fish.

INTENDED DISCOVERY PATH. (1) One demo and the object is free: "~~~~" surface, "####" gravel, "|" stalks growing out of it, "><>" fish. A kid says fish tank; the clue's digits line up with the "|" columns, so the format ("draw my weeds, then put fish in") is readable from two demos. Nothing scores until it is exactly right, which is the first gate. (2) N is not any of the obvious counts: the generator rejection-filters every shipped demo so that N differs from the number of fish, right-facing fish, left-facing fish, fish whose TAIL is against a plant, fish touching a plant at either end, fish touching nothing, plants, plant cells, water rows, fish in the bottom row, fish in the top row, fish in the busiest row, neighbouring same-direction pairs, nose-to-nose pairs, tail-to-tail pairs, plants with a fish beside them, fish minus depth, and fish minus N. (3) The lateral step is that a fish has a POINTY END and the thing it points at matters: only the cell in front of the nose counts, so "><>|" counts and "|><>" does not. Every demo is forced to contain >= 2 fish whose tail is against a plant and >= 2 fish touching nothing, so "any fish next to a plant" is visibly wrong rather than invisibly wrong, and both orientations always appear at least twice. (4) The last clause is the near miss that costs a round: counting nibbling FISH is always 1-3 more than N because every demo carries 1-3 spots eaten from both sides ("><>|<><", two fish kissing the same leaf). A player who fits the demos will see that the fish count never equals N and has to move to counting the leaf instead of the fish; a player who ignores the demos and probes "make the fish count N" scores 0 because clause 3 then fails.

WHY IT SHOULD SIT IN THE BAND. The object is unmistakable (lesson from fennick and garrow: bars and bordered grids are not books and pizzas; "><>" is a fish). The measurement is a relation between two DRAWN things and has no name. The counted thing is anchored to the plant columns, which come from the clue, so no answer transfers between clues and the demo channel cannot be farmed (the LegoZendo/tovel leak). Partial understanding pays: format only ~1 %, clause 2 without clause 3 ~11 %, everything ~100 %.

WITNESS TABLE (600 fresh clues; the attacker is assumed to know the well-formedness format perfectly and to build a legal tank satisfying their hypothesis). random legal tank 1.0 %; TRUE RULE 100 %; N nibbled spots but clause 3 unknown 11.2 %; N nibbled spots with no double 0.0 %; N nibbling FISH (the n-gram reading) 0.0 %; N nibbling fish plus a double 0.0 %; N nibbled plant COLUMNS 5.8 %; N fish 0.0 %; N right-facing 0.2 %; N left-facing 0.3 %; N tail-on-plant 0.7 %; N touching a plant either end 0.0 %; N plants with a fish beside them 1.8 %; N fish in the bottom row 1.5 %; N fish in the top row 1.7 %; N fish in the busiest row 0.3 %; N same-direction neighbour pairs 1.2 %; N nose-to-nose pairs 1.5 %; N tail-to-tail pairs 1.3 %; N water rows 0.0 %. Empty string, junk, the clue echoed back, one fixed answer for every clue, the previous demo reused for the next clue, surface+gravel with no fish, the clue's plant row drawn with no fish, and the real solution with its lines shuffled: all 0.0 %.

VALIDATION. 4000 clues: solve() scores 1 on every one; generate 0.08 ms, solve 9-17 ms, score 0.15 ms (0.024 ms worst on junk incl. 2000-char rubbish). The scorer was cross-checked against an independent re-implementation on 32135 (clue, answer) pairs - real solutions, whitespace/case/reversal variants and structural mutations (flipped fish, moved fish, deleted fish, extra fish, broken plant, dropped row, duplicated row) - with 0 disagreements. solve() varies the depth (4/5/6 = 20/41/39 %), the total fish (8-27), the number of double-nibbled spots (1-3), which rows carry the nibbles and every filler position; the top row carries 1-4 fish; it never emits a minimal witness.

LEVERS IF IT DRIFTS. Too easy: count only the spots that are nibbled from one side, or only the spots on plants taller than 1, or require the double-nibbled spot to be on the tallest plant. Too hard: drop clause 3 (the double) - that alone moves the naive "count the nibbling fish" reading from 0 % to a crack.
